subject.title: refactor: move non-session runtime journals to SQLite

question: Should the shipped ACP and audit diagnostic-access contracts be preserved through SQLite-backed readers, or may this PR intentionally remove them in favor of a newly documented replacement API?
rationale: The storage migration is technically coherent, but choosing whether existing diagnostic handles and operator inspection workflows remain public compatibility contracts requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Preserve diagnostic access
options.body: Add supported SQLite-backed readers or exports and retain compatible result/output handles until a documented deprecation completes.

options.title: Approve a breaking replacement
options.body: Explicitly approve removal, define the replacement inspection workflow, document upgrade impact, and provide real-runtime proof for it.

recommendation.title: Preserve diagnostic access
recommendation.body: Add supported SQLite-backed readers or exports and retain compatible result/output handles until a documented deprecation completes.

likelyOwner.reason: The most concrete blocking compatibility question concerns the ACP parent-stream diagnostic contract tied to their recent area work.
